ingredients_raw: salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Stir the mayonnaise, onion, pickle, and pickle juice together in a bowl. Season with salt, black pepper, and celery salt to taste. Cover, and refrigerate for 1 hour before serving.

review.reviewBody: Right on, SKANDREWS! The tartar sauce of my youth, in WA state, was NEVER a sweet-pickle sauce- it was always dilly. This is almost exactly the same recipe I use- will try it your way soon! Thanks so much for sticking up for the "savory" side! :o)

I mostly followed this, but used dill relish (lazy!) and a touch of regular relish. Added the dill juice plus lots of pepper and some seasoning salt. I was trying really hard not to eat it as chip dip! Very, very good!

This is excellent! I did make a few changes, hence the 4 stars. I halved the recipe, used dill pickle relish (not minced), no juice, no S&P and celery seed instead of celery salt. I took Emma's advice (but used a microplane) to mince the onion. I also added a shake of dill weed and a scant Tbl. of chopped capers. My husband pronounced this as good, if not better than the tartar sauce we get at our favorite British Pub with fish and chips! Thank you for sharing this "not sweet" tartar sauce recipe!!

This is very similar to the tartar sauce I've made for many years. I think dill pickle relish or chopped dill pickle are much better than sweet pickles in tartar sauce. You can also substitute capers, if you like. I use a little less onion and pepper in mine and add a little prepared mustard and no extra pickle juice. I also sometimes add just a pinch of cayenne pepper for an extra layer of flavor. Try it. It's easy to make and tastes great. 

I suggest making it at least an hour in advance if you have time, to allow the flavors to blend. You can make it and store it in the refrigerator several days in advance.

I made a few little changes
3/4 c. mayo & 1/4 c. sour cream,
1/4 c. dill relish w/ some extra juice, 
green onion & a few capers (optional)
1/2 tea. dill weed .. Perfect

I wanted to use this sauce right away so I minced the onion very, very and I mean very fine, until it was almost liquefied! No need to wait for the flavors to blend or mellow when doing this. I used pickle relish as that is what I had on hand. A bit of celery seed was substituted for celery salt for the same reason. This is an excellent homemade tartar sauce!

I make this all the time now. No need to buy store bought ever again...I do add cayenne pepper, horseradish, dry mustard, & extra dill pickle juice. No salt, celery salt, or minced onion just because it isn't necessary for me. We LOVE it!!!!
I am not a huge fan of mayo so I used greek yogurt instead. Otherwise I followed the recipe as is and it was lick the bowl delicious!

Very nice tartar sauce. I used minced onion and dried celery seeds since I didn't have celery salt. Made this the night before and served with some fish sticks. Hubs loved it, and I enjoyed it too. It isn't sweet and is a very easy recipe to make, so I'm happy. :) It does make more than we needed for the two of us, but I expect it to last for a bit in the fridge so we'll have some fish again in a few days. Thanks for the recipe!

2 things to be aware of:
1. If you adjust the recipe, the pickle juice calculation is way off (the error is blatant enough to be noticed, but kind of a pain if you don't remember the original amount)
2: Salt - My pickle juice must have had a TON of salt in it. I added only a dash of celery salt, and 2 grinds from a salt mill, and it was WAY too salty. Had to add about 1/4 more mayo to the already halved recipe to cut it.

I do like the dill vs. sweet pickle relish. I also added some dried dill to detract from the saltiness. Will definitely taste before adding any salt or celery salt next time.
I blended everything in a food processor. My family loved it with cob nuggets. Will definitely make it again.

This is a great recipe, and simple to make. I have made it exactly to your directions and everyone loved it! Now, I stepped it up a little and put in about (I didn't measure but went by taste), a tablespoon of yellow mustard this time, and it gives it just a little bite. A regular for fish, but I love it with fries as well!
Delicious and so easy to make. I will never get the store bought stuff any longer. Thank you for the recipe.

Was a little short on the mayo, so I added some Miracle Whip which I think gave this tartar sauce a little extra tang. The celery salt is important in this recipe, so I’d recommend not skipping it. My husband flipped over this, and I think this now will be our go-to for tartar sauce. Served with some simple salmon patties, mac and cheese, and sliced tomatoes.
SO good... added some whole Dijon mustard seed and Celery seed... over the top!
Absolutely delicious. Best I have had in a very long time.
Cajun husband said better than mom's!!

Wow unexpected, I added dill and used miracle whip and it came out really good!

Thanks for this!

This is the same tartar sauce my mother made also. It is what I measure all other attempts by. They have all fallen short: too sweet, too many extraneous ingredients, bland. There were 7 children, so her cooking motto was KISS. It was always simple and delicous! Great with the Old Fashioned onion rings also. Can't go wrong!
Tastes great
